tests.description: Reference: WRF 4.8 em_scm_xy single-column run (GNU gfortran 13.3 REAL*4 build, dt = 60 s, damp_opt = 2 dampcoef = 0.003 zdamp = 5000 m, pert_coriolis = .true., use_theta_m = 1, hybrid_opt = 0; data/eqwefic/scm_dyn, the scm_ref namelist re-run with the instrumented binary) dumped by the ctessum-claude/WRF fork, branch earthsciml-instrumented, commit 83347b2 (dyn_em/module_em.F rk_tendency, rk_step 1 of the step; module_esm_dump), merged with the same step's radiation subassembly dump and the wrfout eta grid by tools/merge_dumps.py into data/eqwefic/dumps/dyn_column/esm_dump_dyn_suite_<step>.json. The rebuilt binary reproduces the archived scm_ref radiation subassembly dumps bit for bit (all but the three B9 variables). The column is horizontally uniform (u, v identical in the two tile columns, ww = 0, all map factors 1, c1 = 1, c2 = 0). Expected tendencies are the dumped mass-coupled increments of the named routine divided by the coupling mass of their grid point (muu, muv, mut), i.e. the instantaneous decoupled rate at the time-level-n state; references are single precision, so tolerances follow the rel 1e-5 real32 convention, with absolute Linf bounds on whole profiles where values pass through zero. Routine: curvature, normal-code branch (dyn_em/module_big_step_utilities_em.F:4175-4469); the vxgm map-factor-gradient terms are identically zero in this column. The eta interpolation weights are the dumped fnm/fnp. Measured residual over the three regimes (zero tolerance): Linf <= 1.2e-11 m/s^2 in du_dt and <= 5.5e-12 in dv_dt (values <= 5e-10, <= 9e-10), <= 2.1e-11 in dw_dt (values 1.41e-5, <= 1.5e-6 relative). These are NOT transcription errors but the resolution of the reference: the dump records each routine's contribution as the difference of the single-precision tendency array across the call, and curvature is added onto a tendency that already holds the Coriolis (and, for w, the pressure-gradient-plus-buoyancy) term of O(40) in mass-coupled units, so a ~3e-5 coupled increment is quantized to one ulp of 40, 3.8e-6, i.e. 4.8e-11 m/s^2 after dividing by mu = 79265 Pa (the level-1 u increment, ~1e-6 coupled, even rounds to exactly 0). Linf bounds are therefore set at that quantization limit, abs 5e-11 m/s^2; the w term, far above it, is also asserted pointwise at rel 1e-5. A sign error or a missing term moves each tendency by its full value (up to 9e-10 in u and v, 1.4e-5 in w) and fails. Regime: step 60 (t = 1 h, early afternoon, convective boundary layer).
